commons:3078150.summary: The Virgin sits enthroned in a deep blue robe, holding the Christ Child, who sits upright on her lap in a golden-brown garment with his own halo. Two soldier saints, Theodore and George, stand guard on either side holding crosses, while behind the throne two angels turn their faces upward. Painted in hot wax, the icon contrasts the still, frontal saints with the lively, almost classical angels, and is one of the rare icons to survive from before Byzantine Iconoclasm.
facts: Saint Catherine's Monastery is the only place where a substantial group of pre-iconoclastic encaustic icons survives, some dating as early as the 6th century.
No panel icons earlier than the few 6th-century examples preserved at Sinai survive in their original state.
commons:3078150.notes: 'Encaustic Virgin' is only the Commons file name; title supplied from the Commons description ('Virgin and Child with angels and Sts. George and Theodore'). Which saint stands on which side was not confirmed from a reliable source. Place of production is not documented.

cur:catacombs-bode-christ-relief-constan.summary: Under an ornate architrave on twisted columns, a youthful Christ stands frontally between two apostles, his right hand raised. The relief was carved in Constantinople by reworking an older pagan columnar sarcophagus from Dokimeion in Asia Minor, a striking example of the Christian transformation of classical monuments.
facts: The museum states that it was acquired in Istanbul in 1899 (inv. 2430).
The original 3rd-century sarcophagus came from the marble workshops of Dokimeion in Phrygia.

cur:manuscripts-drogo-last-supper-arrest.summary: The letter D holds two scenes of Holy Thursday: above, Christ sits with the apostles at a long table for the Last Supper; below, Judas kisses Christ while soldiers with spears and torches crowd in to seize him. The tiny figures within the initial compress the whole night of the betrayal into one letter.
facts: The Drogo Sacramentary was written and painted for the personal use of Drogo, Bishop of Metz and a son of Charlemagne; it contains only the prayers spoken by the bishop at Mass through the year.
Its scenes are set inside the initial letters of the prayers, in delicate gold vine-scrolls — an early and influential use of the historiated initial.
cur:manuscripts-drogo-last-supper-arrest.notes: Folio not stated on the Commons file; the miniature is an initial within the text page.

vam:O87639.summary: In the upper scene the three Magi, in Phrygian caps and carrying bowls of gifts, approach the Virgin, who sits with the Christ Child on her lap while Joseph stands behind; the guiding star appears in the border above. Below, in the Presentation in the Temple, Mary holds out the Child over an altar to the aged Simeon, who receives him with veiled hands, while Joseph carries two doves. Both scenes unfold before townscapes of tiled roofs, carved in deep relief with a real sense of movement.
facts: The V&A notes that the buildings are closely modelled on the architecture of the Utrecht Psalter (about 820).
Plaques like this seem to have served as models for 10th-century manuscript painting in Anglo-Saxon England, as has been shown for the Benedictional of St Æthelwold (V&A).
Holes in the corners were probably for attachment to a book cover.
vam:O87639.notes: V&A: North-East France (probably Lorraine/Metz), late 9th century.
